skill.name: code-validation-sandbox
skill.description: Validates educational code examples with layer-aware strategies, sandbox setup, and language-specific checks for Python-focused chapters.
skill.summary: Layer-aware validation for educational code examples.
skill.author: 92Bilal26

security_audit.summary: The skill has legitimate educational code validation goals, but several execution paths are unsafe for untrusted content. Confirmed risks include remote installer pipe-to-shell commands, unsafe eval of chapter-derived context, and host execution of extracted Markdown Python code. Many Markdown code-fence and documentation matches were false positives.

remediation.issue: Remote installers are piped directly into sh or bash during sandbox setup.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell installers with pinned package versions, checksum verification, or official package manager steps.

remediation.issue: validate.sh evaluates context variables derived from chapter files.
remediation.suggestion: Remove eval and parse only whitelisted keys with strict value validation for layer, language, tier, and depth.

remediation.issue: Python code extracted from Markdown can run on the host interpreter.
remediation.suggestion: Run extracted code only inside a locked-down container with read-only mounts, no secrets, no network, and resource limits.

remediation.issue: Docker setup can use a user-selected base image while mounting the workspace.
remediation.suggestion: Use an allowlist of trusted images and mount the workspace read-only unless write access is required.

static_findings.snippet: - [ ] Did I analyze layer context? (Not same depth for all)
- [ ] Did I use language-appropriate tools? (Not Python AST on JavaScript)
- [ ] Did I provide actionable diagnostics? (Not just "error on line X")
- [ ] Did I verify claims (L2)? (Not trust "3x faster" without measurement)
- [ ] Did I test reusability (L3)? (Not single example only)
- [ ] Did I test integration (L4)? (Not happy path only)

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Evaluation of Chapter-Derived Context Variables
semantic_findings.description: validate.sh evaluates context assignments produced from chapter files. The layer value can originate from chapter-meta.yaml, so malicious metadata can become shell syntax.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The data flow is direct: chapter metadata is emitted as shell assignments and then evaluated. This is a classic command injection risk when chapter content is untrusted.

semantic_findings.title: Host Execution of Extracted Markdown Code
semantic_findings.description: validate-python.sh extracts Python blocks from Markdown and executes them with the host python3 interpreter. This bypasses the sandbox promise for untrusted chapter content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script extracts Markdown code into files and invokes python3 on those files. A malicious code block would run with the permissions of the user running validation.

semantic_findings.title: Writable Workspace Exposed During Network-Based Setup
semantic_findings.description: setup-sandbox.sh bind mounts the current workspace into a Docker container and then runs network-sourced installers inside that environment. A compromised installer could modify workspace files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The bind mount and installer execution are both explicit in the setup script. The impact depends on Docker permissions and installer behavior, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.user_title: Validate Teaching Code Examples in Sandboxes
content.value_statement: Code examples in lessons can fail silently or mislead readers. This skill detects context, selects validation depth, and reports actionable issues.
actual_capabilities: Detects lesson layer from metadata and Markdown content signals.
Detects Python, Node.js, Rust, and Go evidence in chapter files.
Selects validation depth for manual, collaboration, skill, or integration chapters.
Extracts Python code blocks from Markdown and checks syntax and runtime behavior.
Creates a Docker container with Python and Node tooling for validation work.
Reports validation failures with severity-oriented messages.
limitations: Node, Rust, and Go validation scripts are referenced but not included.
Python runtime checks execute extracted code and need trusted input or isolation.
Sandbox setup downloads installers from external URLs during setup.
This skill is not for production deployment testing or security certification.

use_cases.title: Validate lesson code before publication
use_cases.description: Check syntax and runtime behavior for code examples in educational chapters.

use_cases.title: Review AI-assisted examples
use_cases.description: Verify that baseline and optimized examples still produce equivalent behavior.

use_cases.title: Assess generated code blocks
use_cases.description: Run context-aware checks before adding generated examples to training material.

prompt_templates.title: Validate one chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this chapter directory with default layer detection. Report critical syntax or runtime issues first. Path: {{chapter_path}}

prompt_templates.title: Force a validation layer
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate validation when the layer is already known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this chapter as Layer {{layer}} content. Explain the selected checks and summarize the highest priority fixes. Path: {{chapter_path}}

prompt_templates.title: Check AI collaboration claims
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for before and after examples.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the baseline and optimized examples in this chapter. Confirm equivalent behavior and flag unsupported performance claims. Path: {{chapter_path}}

prompt_templates.title: Audit integration content
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this Layer 4 chapter for integration readiness. Check service assumptions, missing health checks, and recovery coverage. Path: {{chapter_path}}

output_examples.input: A Layer 1 Python chapter with multiple beginner code examples.
output_examples.output: The report lists total blocks, one critical runtime error, and a direct fix for the failing example.

output_examples.input: A Layer 2 chapter that claims an optimized version is faster.
output_examples.output: The report confirms both versions run, compares their behavior, and flags any unsupported performance claim.

output_examples.input: A Layer 4 chapter that describes several services.
output_examples.output: The report identifies missing integration evidence and recommends health checks before publication.

best_practices: Run validation in an isolated container when chapter content is untrusted.
Review the selected layer and language before accepting validation results.
Treat runtime failures as publication blockers for beginner-facing examples.
anti_patterns: Do not run extracted code from unknown sources on the host machine.
Do not assume Node, Rust, or Go validation is complete without adding scripts.
Do not trust performance claims without measured evidence.

faq.question: What does this skill validate?
faq.answer: It validates educational code examples and selects checks based on lesson context.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it validate JavaScript or Rust today?
faq.answer: It can detect those languages, but the matching validation scripts are not included.

faq.question: Is the sandbox fully isolated?
faq.answer: No. Some Python validation runs extracted code with the host Python interpreter.

faq.question: Should I use it for production deployment tests?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that it is not for production deployment testing.

faq.question: What should authors fix first?
faq.answer: Authors should remove pipe-to-shell setup commands and avoid eval on chapter-derived data.
